rationale: The paper is a policy and institutional review of water and sanitation service delivery in Malawi combining documentary analysis, secondary national survey tabulations (2005 Integrated Household Survey and 2006 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey), and qualitative interviews. All quantitative figures reported—such as national/urban/rural water and sanitation coverage percentages (Tables 2–3), sector budget shares (Table 4), and mean production cost versus tariff per litre—are purely descriptive secondary statistics with zero inferential hypothesis tests, regressions, standard errors, confidence intervals, or p-values.
